chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Wasshash, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamzah, he raised it (to the Imam) and said:

He said: 'Do not eat the meat of a lamb that suckled from the milk of a sow.' Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: 'All these narrations are understood to mean that if it suckled from the sow a complete suckling period, its flesh and blood grow from it and its strength becomes firm because of that. But if it was a single feeding or less than what causes the flesh to grow and the bone to strengthen, there is no harm in eating its meat after its purification, as we will mention, God willing. And the first hadith explicitly stated this when the questioner asked him, and he said: It suckled from a sow until it grew up and its bone became firm, so he answered him at that time with what we mentioned. And that which indicates this is what he narrated:'

key_terms.يَنْبُتُ عَلَيْهِ: Grows upon it / is derived from it

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating meat from an animal that suckled from a pig?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi clarifies that the prohibition is not absolute but contingent upon the duration of suckling; if the lamb suckles long enough for its flesh and blood to be transformed by the pig's milk, it is impure, whereas brief suckling does not alter its nature. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic principle of *istibra'* (purification/verification) and demonstrates how scholars reconcile apparent contradictions in hadith by examining the degree of physical transformation rather than mere ingestion.
